entries.meaning: A small metal box with a lock for holding money. ---
examples: The bake sale money is in the cash box.
Somebody walked off with the cash box.
Count the cash box before you close up.

entries.meaning: A locking box for valuables or keys. ---
examples: The house key is in a lockbox by the door.
He keeps the deed in a lockbox at the bank.
Real estate agents put lockboxes on every listing.

entries.meaning: A heavy metal box built to protect money and documents. ---
examples: The payroll rode in a strongbox under the seat.
The fire took everything but the strongbox.
He bolted the strongbox to the floor.

entries.meaning: A flat sturdy trunk kept at the foot of a bed, common in the military. ---
examples: Everything he owned fit in one footlocker.
The footlocker is full of old uniforms.
Footlockers lined both sides of the barracks.

entries.meaning: A shallow box of absorbent granules where a cat relieves itself. ---
examples: Somebody needs to clean the litter box.
The litter box is in the laundry room.
Two cats can share one litter box, barely.
entries.contrast: American; the British say litter tray.

entries.meaning: A small container, often shaped like a pig, for saving coins. ---
examples: He emptied his piggy bank to buy the game.
There's about four dollars in the piggy bank.
Every grandchild got a piggy bank.

entries.meaning: A shallow dish for cigarette ash and butts. ---
examples: The ashtray on the porch is overflowing.
He tapped his cigarette on the edge of the ashtray.
Old cars had ashtrays in every door.

entries.meaning: Planter has 2 distinct senses.
examples: There are planters on either side of the front door.
She filled the planter with geraniums.
The clay planter cracked over the winter.
The planter puts down twelve rows at a time.
He calibrated the planter before starting.
New planters cost as much as a house.

senses.head: A decorative container that plants grow in
examples: There are planters on either side of the front door.
She filled the planter with geraniums.
The clay planter cracked over the winter.

senses.head: A machine that drops seed into the ground at even spacing
examples: The planter puts down twelve rows at a time.
He calibrated the planter before starting.
New planters cost as much as a house.

entries.meaning: A protective cover that snaps around a cell phone. ---
examples: The phone case saved the screen.
He keeps a credit card in his phone case.
They sell phone cases by the register.

entries.meaning: A stiff or soft case that protects eyeglasses. ---
examples: Her glasses case was empty.
Put your readers back in the glasses case.
There are three glasses cases in the junk drawer.

entries.meaning: A padded case made to protect and carry one particular item. ---
examples: The drill came with a hard plastic carrying case.
She zipped the laptop into its carrying case.
Both carrying cases have foam inserts.

entries.meaning: A long zippered bag that a suit or dress travels in. ---
examples: His tuxedo is in a garment bag in the closet.
She hung the garment bag on the hook in the car.
Airlines let you carry a garment bag on board.

entries.meaning: A soft bag for workout clothes and shoes. ---
examples: His gym bag has been in the trunk all week.
She stuffed a towel in her gym bag.
The locker room was full of gym bags.

entries.meaning: A small zippered pouch for cosmetics. ---
examples: Everything spilled out of her makeup bag.
The makeup bag fits in a carry-on.
She has separate makeup bags for travel and home.

entries.meaning: A small bag for a toothbrush, razor, and other travel toiletries. ---
examples: Pack your toiletry bag last.
The toiletry bag hangs on the back of the door.
Hotel toiletry bags always smell like soap.

entries.meaning: A flat bag with a long strap worn across the body. ---
examples: He rides to work with a messenger bag across his chest.
Her laptop fits in the messenger bag.
Messenger bags were everywhere on campus.

entries.meaning: A cloth sack that closes by pulling two cords. ---
examples: The team handed out drawstring bags at the game.
She carries her shoes in a drawstring bag.
The drawstring bag doubles as a backpack.

entries.meaning: A simple bag with shoulder straps for carrying supplies on your back. ---
examples: He set off with a knapsack and a canteen.
Her knapsack held two days of food.
The knapsacks were piled at the trailhead.
entries.contrast: The k is silent: NAP-sak. Most Americans now say backpack.

entries.meaning: Pet carrier has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The cat howled in the pet carrier the whole way.
Your pet carrier has to fit under the seat.
Both pet carriers are out in the garage.
The cat hates going in the pet carrier.
Airlines have size limits for pet carriers.
Put a towel in the pet carrier so she's comfortable.

senses.head: A ventilated box or bag for transporting a cat or small dog
examples: The cat howled in the pet carrier the whole way.
Your pet carrier has to fit under the seat.
Both pet carriers are out in the garage.

senses.head: A small box or bag with air holes for carrying an animal
examples: The cat hates going in the pet carrier.
Airlines have size limits for pet carriers.
Put a towel in the pet carrier so she's comfortable.

entries.meaning: The big plastic container with a handle that milk is sold in. ---
examples: There's half a milk jug left.
We rinse out milk jugs and use them for watering.
He drank straight from the milk jug.
entries.contrast: In the US this is the gallon container from the store; in Britain a milk jug is a small pitcher for the table.

entries.meaning: A large container with a handle for carrying drinking water. ---
examples: The team keeps a water jug on the bench.
Fill the water jug before we leave.
Two five-gallon water jugs sat by the door.

entries.meaning: A flat metal or plastic bottle carried on a strap or belt. ---
examples: He took a long drink from his canteen.
Her canteen was empty by noon.
Every scout carried a canteen.
entries.contrast: In American English a canteen is a water flask; in Britain it is usually a workplace cafeteria.

entries.meaning: A slim curved bottle for carrying liquor in a pocket. ---
examples: He had a hip flask in his coat.
She gave him an engraved hip flask.
Hip flasks aren't allowed in the stadium.

entries.meaning: A large glass jug used to carry draft beer home from a brewery. ---
examples: He filled a growler at the taproom.
Bring your own growler and save two dollars.
There are two empty growlers in the fridge.

entries.meaning: A heavy mug for beer, often with a hinged lid. ---
examples: He drank out of a ceramic stein.
The shelf was lined with painted steins.
A full stein holds about a liter.
entries.contrast: Rhymes with fine, not with green.

entries.meaning: A drinking glass with a stem and a wide bowl. ---
examples: Water goblets were set at every place.
She poured the wine into a heavy goblet.
The goblet was etched with a family crest.

entries.meaning: A large stemmed cup, especially one used in a church service. ---
examples: The priest raised the chalice.
A silver chalice sat on the altar.
The museum displayed two medieval chalices.
entries.contrast: The ch sounds like church, not like k.

entries.meaning: A glass bottle that wine or liquor is poured into for serving. ---
examples: He poured the scotch from a crystal decanter.
Let the wine sit in the decanter for an hour.
Two decanters stood on the sideboard.

entries.meaning: A thick pottery jar used for cooking or storing food. ---
examples: The beans simmered all day in a crock.
Pickles used to be put up in a stoneware crock.
She had crocks of butter down in the cellar.

entries.meaning: An insulated mug with a lid that keeps a drink hot in the car. ---
examples: He filled his travel mug before the drive.
The travel mug fits in the cup holder.
There are four travel mugs in the cabinet.

entries.meaning: A toddler's cup with a lid and a spout that keeps it from spilling. ---
examples: She left her sippy cup under the car seat.
The sippy cup leaked all over the diaper bag.
We have six sippy cups and no matching lids.

entries.meaning: A disposable cup made of coated paper. ---
examples: Coffee came in a paper cup with a plastic lid.
Rinse and stack the paper cups.
The paper cup went soft at the bottom.

entries.meaning: A cheap disposable or reusable cup made of plastic. ---
examples: They served punch in red plastic cups.
A plastic cup of soda tipped over on the table.
We bought a sleeve of plastic cups for the party.

entries.meaning: A cup for coffee, whether china or paper. ---
examples: There's a coffee cup ring on the desk.
He carried two coffee cups up the stairs.
The coffee cup was still warm.

entries.meaning: A cardboard band around a hot cup so it doesn't burn your hand. ---
examples: The barista slid a coffee sleeve onto the cup.
Ask for a coffee sleeve — that thing is scalding.
Coffee sleeves pile up in my car.

entries.meaning: The molded holder in a car or chair that keeps a drink upright. ---
examples: Stick your soda in the cup holder.
The van has twelve cup holders.
Something sticky spilled in the cup holder.

entries.meaning: Spout has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Tea dripped from the spout.
The spout on the gas can is missing.
Both watering cans have long spouts.
Water dribbles down the outside of the spout.
The tub spout pulls up to switch to the shower.
These faucets come with taller spouts.

senses.head: The narrow opening that a container pours through
examples: Tea dripped from the spout.
The spout on the gas can is missing.
Both watering cans have long spouts.

senses.head: The part of a faucet or tap that the water pours out of
examples: Water dribbles down the outside of the spout.
The tub spout pulls up to switch to the shower.
These faucets come with taller spouts.

entries.meaning: A container that releases its contents a little at a time. ---
examples: The soap dispenser is empty.
There's a tape dispenser on the desk.
They installed water dispensers in the hallway.

entries.meaning: Spigot has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Hook the hose to the spigot on the side of the house.
Beer ran from the spigot into the pitcher.
The outdoor spigots freeze every winter.
Hook the hose up to the spigot on the side of the house.
The spigot drips no matter how hard you crank it.
There are spigots front and back.

senses.head: A tap on a barrel or an outdoor faucet
examples: Hook the hose to the spigot on the side of the house.
Beer ran from the spigot into the pitcher.
The outdoor spigots freeze every winter.

senses.head: An outdoor tap that a garden hose screws onto
examples: Hook the hose up to the spigot on the side of the house.
The spigot drips no matter how hard you crank it.
There are spigots front and back.

entries.contrast: A mostly American word; the British say tap.

entries.meaning: One of the plastic loops that hold six cans together.
examples: Cut the six-pack rings before you throw them out.
A six-pack ring can choke a seabird.
The cans pulled free of the six-pack ring.
